title: 'We Are Competing With Disney': Netflix's The One Piece Anime Remake Updates Its 'Old Story' for a New Generation, Producer Says
snippet: The long-awaited One Piece anime remake is updating its nearly 30-year-old story for a younger generation with its upcoming Netflix release.

The latest update on The One Piece comes from George Wada, the co-founder and CEO of Wit Studio, which is handling the new anime remake for Netflix. Per an interview with the YouTube Channel, Ai Show, Wada revealed why Eiichiro Oda's ongoing story is being remade, even as the current anime adaptation by Toei Animation continues. Wada also acknowledged the incredible growth the anime industry is seeing worldwide and the new challenges that come with, such as keeping up with Hollywood and Disney. Netflix’s One Piece Remake Aims to Captivate a New Generation "The reason we decided to remake One Piece is something the author, Eiichiro Oda, said," Wada explained. "He said that One Piece has become very long and full of details, since it started so long ago. The new generation watching modern productions may not feel the same excitement towards the old animation." "He felt a bit of regret about that and wanted the new generation to know and follow the story. That motivated me to remake this great story using modern techniques suitable for today's audience." Despite being a worldwide phenomenon, One Piece's nearly 30-year history is often seen as intimidating for new readers, especially when it comes to the original anime. When One Piece returns this April for "The Elbaph Arc," it will resume with Episode 1156. It's why the live-action One Piece series on Netflix has seen incredible success, attracting new viewers simply by being in the double digits rather than four. Netflix and Shonen Jump owner, Shueisha, are trying to make lightning strike twice by delivering a new One Piece anime that's easy to jump into for arguably the largest streaming platform worldwide. "I believe companies like Netflix have changed the landscape," Wada said. "We now realize that our works are watched worldwide." "We are no longer competing only within Japan; we are competing with global giants like Hollywood and Disney. These works are seen by people all over the world. So, improving production methods and continuous development have become essential." When The One Piece was first unveiled to the world in December 2023, Netflix emphasized the use of cutting-edge technology to set the new anime apart from its predecessor. However, to many One Piece fans, the vague use of "cutting-edge visual technology" sounded like a dog whistle for AI-animated programs -- something that Wit Studio had previously experimented with in its three-minute short film, The Dog & the Boy. Despite the company's previous use, Wada and Wit Studio currently see AI as a "threat," rather than a potential solution to the anime industry's current production problems. "I believe it has become a threat," he said. "We carry the responsibility of protecting creators -- artists, animators, and others and many legal issues are still unresolved. So, we are watching these changes carefully to understand their future impact on the industry." Currently, Netflix's The One Piece has yet to announce an official release date. However, Oda confirmed at Jump Festa 2026 that its production is "progressing steadily."
